html:
A city on the south coast of China, at the mouth of the Pearl River, ruled by Britain from 1842 to 1997 and now a special region of China. It grew from a few fishing villages into one of the world's great ports and money centres.

Britain took Hong Kong Island after the First Opium War under the Treaty of Nanking of 1842. Kowloon followed in 1860, and in 1898 the New Territories were leased for 99 years. As a free port it handled much of China's foreign trade, and HSBC was founded there in 1865. During the plague of 1894 the germ that causes plague was identified in the city.

Japan occupied it from 1941 to 1945. After the communist victory in 1949, refugees from the mainland poured in, and their labour built a boom in textiles, toys and electronics. The film star Bruce Lee grew up there. In the 1970s and 1980s it held camps for Vietnamese boat people. When China opened its economy, the Shenzhen economic zone was placed right across the border to draw on Hong Kong's money and know-how.

When the lease ran out, Britain handed the whole territory back on 1 July 1997, under the formula "one country, two systems". China promised Hong Kong its own laws and freedoms for fifty years. Large protests in 2019 were followed by a national security law in 2020 that ended most open opposition.
sum: A city on the south coast of China, at the mouth of the Pearl River, ruled by Britain from 1842 to 1997 and now a special region of China. It grew from a few fishing villages into one of the world's great ports and money centres.
